content.comment_body: SSA-783481: Denial-of-Service vulnerability found in [product_name] hardware version [version_no]. An attacker may cause a device crash if a user loads a malicious project file. The problem relates to the hardware component. [company_name] has released new hardware versions for the affected [product_name] product families where this issue has been resolved. Updates for other product lines are in progress. More details are provided in the chapter 'Additional Information.' Further information can be found in the related support article: [url]. Affected versions currently do not have a planned fix; customers are advised to follow recommended workarounds and mitigations, such as limiting the possibility to run untrusted code and adhering to general security guidelines. [company_name] advises protecting network access with appropriate security measures and configuring the environment according to operational guidelines available via [url]. The vulnerability, CVE-2020-25236, allows the control logic of [product_name] devices to be manipulated so the device must be manually reset after a crash. This vulnerability has a CVSS 3.1 base score of 5.5, relating to improper handling of exceptional conditions. The advisory acknowledges [user_name] for responsible disclosure. A list of hardware versions and article numbers that are now fixed is provided in 'Additional Information,' all referenced by [article_no]. Updates and history data are documented, along with terms of use available at [url]. For further inquiries regarding security vulnerabilities in [company_name] products, contact ProductCERT at [url].
Educational settings may face challenges with this vulnerability. In my experience, some students might go to great lengths to interfere with systems during exams.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are expressing concern over a denial-of-service vulnerability in a specific [product_name] hardware version, where loading malicious project files can disrupt operations. There is no fix planned for certain versions, leaving some environments—especially those with less control over device access, such as educational institutions—more susceptible to risk. Manual reset is required after incidents, affecting both reliability and security. While [company_name] has released improved hardware for newer devices, older ones remain vulnerable.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [company_name] hardware to be secure against denial-of-service attacks, even in environments where access is less restricted. They are hoping for a fix or at least effective mitigation strategies, seeking more robust protection, especially in sensitive use cases like educational institutions.
pain_keywords: no fix planned for older versions
